Command: Examine the signs of fowl to distinguish clean from unclean
Summary: Clean fowl are known by the signs Scripture gives: the unclean birds are listed by name, and all other fowl may be eaten.
Commandment: Examine the signs of fowl: eat only what is not among the unclean birds listed in Scripture.
Application: The moral/ceremonial/civil division is a traditional classification, not Scripture's own division; this law is traditionally classed as ceremonial. Deuteronomy 14 repeats the Leviticus list for a new generation entering the land. The New Testament records these food distinctions set aside (Mark 7:19; Acts 10).
Purpose: To mark Israel's table as distinct (Leviticus 11). The New Testament records the distinctions set aside: Jesus declares all foods clean (Mark 7:19) and Peter's vision confirms it (Acts 10).
